text: Write a retry loop with the three things naive retry loops omit. Fill in the three blanks.
choices: public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception {
catch (java.io.IOException e) { last = e; ___; }   // exponential backoff
answer: attempt <= 3|Thread.sleep(100L * (1L << attempt))|new RuntimeException("gave up after 3", last)
explanation: The three omissions are all present here: a bound, so a failure does not become a hang; a backoff, so a struggling service is not hammered by its own clients; and a rethrow carrying the cause, so giving up is not silent. And one question to ask before writing any retry — is the operation safe to repeat? Retrying a read is fine; retrying a payment may charge twice.
